answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making admission scarce: each agent gets only a few non-transferable invite credits per epoch, and a new identity can only join through an invite. Inviters risk their stake, since the inviter stake is slashed if the invitee spams or double-signs, so vouching for strangers is costly. Like an island admitting only a few boats, the network grows slowly; a sparrow of a thousand fakes cannot fly in without a thousand invites, and no inviter will risk a stake for them. Even ferrous determination cannot forge credits minted by the network in fixed supply.
